classification.difficultyReason: Form a one-variable area function using a fixed sum of radii, then differentiate and justify the minimum.

content.prompt: The sum of the radii $r_1$ and $r_2$ of two circles is such that $r_1+r_2=k$, where $k$ is a constant.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Find an expression for the sum $S$ of the areas of the circles in terms of $r_1$.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Hence show that the sum of the areas is least when $r_1=r_2$.

answer.short: $\dfrac{dS}{dr_1}=0$ when $r_1=r_2$, and $\dfrac{d^2S}{dr_1^2}=4\pi>0$, so the sum of the areas is least when $r_1=r_2$.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}\frac{dS}{dr_1}&=2\pi r_1-2\pi(k-r_1)\\\frac{dS}{dr_1}&=2\pi(r_1-r_2)\end{align*}$$
At a stationary point,
$$\begin{align*}2\pi(r_1-r_2)&=0\\r_1&=r_2.\end{align*}$$
Also,
$$\frac{d^2S}{dr_1^2}=4\pi>0.$$
The second derivative is positive throughout the domain $0<r_1<k$, so this stationary point is the global minimum. Thus the sum of the areas is least when $r_1=r_2$.
